audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer rows 4-5, 6 and first item read 'Skill' and the 2+ items row read 'Veigar', while content win[N] read Brand on all seven.
audit.why: packet.levelChart is Brand on every row and 53.66% over 369 games agrees. Veigar has no dash and no sustain; his only lane CC is a 20s rank-1 Event Horizon that stuns on its edge only. The existing phases[6].why already describes Brand detonating teamfights, so the Veigar row contradicted its own sentence.
audit.corrected: Rows 4-5, 6, first item and 2+ items moved to Brand, matching the content layer, the packet and the whys already on the page.

audit.whatIsWrong: The late-game text and spikes[3] describe his execute as 'Dark Matter'.
audit.why: Primordial Burst (R) is the execute-flavoured nuke, 120/90/60s at 650 range, and it scales on the target's missing health. Dark Matter is his W — a delayed area drop at 950 whose cooldown is cut by Phenomenal Evil stacks, not an execute. The spike that matters to Brand is the 120s rank-1 R plus whatever stacks he has banked.
audit.corrected: Renamed to Primordial Burst throughout, with the 120s cooldown and the missing-health scaling stated.
sources: enemyKit R and W text and cooldowns

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] calls Primordial Burst his Q, wants.you[3] calls his passive 'mana-into-AP', and breakdown.cooldowns carried no number.
audit.why: Baleful Strike is Q (1000 range, 6s down to 4s) and it is what banks permanent AP off kills; Phenomenal Evil Power grants AP for striking champions and for takedowns, with no mana involved. Event Horizon is 20/18.5/17/15.5/14s at 725 range and stuns only on the perimeter — the single most useful number in the lane and it was absent. Brand's Sear still needs an ablaze target, so E leads every trade.
audit.corrected: Slot names corrected, the passive described accurately, and Event Horizon's 20s rank-1 cooldown written into the cooldown field.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two Do's/Don'ts bodies were the tradeGood/tradeBad strings under unrelated titles (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED), and whys[0]/whys[1] called the first two levels an even skill matchup on rows the chart gives to Brand.
audit.why: The row and the sentence under it were arguing different verdicts, which is the exact defect the chart rule exists to stop.
audit.corrected: Bleed bullets rewritten to their own titles; the first two whys rewritten to argue for the Brand rows they sit under.

edits.before: - Veigar Event Horizon (Cage): matchup-defining — Only the cage EDGE stuns — hold position near the center or leave before it forms; never dash into the wall. It governs your forward steps. - E-Q stun package spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Event Horizon is 20s at rank 1, 14s maxed, 725 range, and only its EDGE stuns — stand near the middle or leave before it forms. - Primordial Burst is 120s at rank 1 and grows with the health you are missing. - Dark Matter has no fixed cooldown; his stacks shorten it. - Your Q is 8s.

edits.before: Veigar wins by landing Event Horizon (Cage), denying your pattern, and out-ranging your plan one polite trade at a time.
edits.after: Veigar wins by catching you on the cage edge and following it with a Primordial Burst that grows with your missing health.

edits.before: If Veigar takes first blood, tighten up: Event Horizon (Cage) is now always up in your head. A second kill means the duel is over and the game isn’t — farm with W-E clears and stay relevant through stun-burn peel.
edits.after: If Veigar takes first blood his passive banks permanent AP off it — deny stacks by clearing from max range instead of dueling. A second kill means the lane is over and the game isn't: farm with W-E and stay relevant as stun-burn peel.

edits.before: Carry through AoE math — no burst mage damages three targets like Brand; your job is the spacing that lets the bounces vote.
edits.after: He has no dash, so Pyroclasm's bounces and slow always land — carry by holding the wave outside 725 and punishing every cage whiff.

edits.before: E the instant ablaze, Q the stun, W the stunned body, walk — the full package chunks half a bar and the burn writes the receipt.
edits.after: Sear stuns only an ablaze target, so E leads — and holding that threat is what keeps an immobile Veigar off his 1000-range Q line.

edits.before: Veigar whiffs Event Horizon (Cage) and the lane briefly belongs to you.
edits.after: Blaze ticks 4 seconds after your last cast — step out and let it finish.

edits.before: W-poking on cooldown with Q unbanked while his engage is loaded — Brand without the stun threat is a bonfire waiting for company.
edits.after: Primordial Burst scales with the health you are missing — at half a bar inside 650 you are the precise target his 120s ultimate wants.

edits.before: Level 1: both champs are limited to basic pokes and neither has a real edge yet, so it's an even skill matchup.
edits.after: Level 1: your 1050-range Q reaches past his 1000 Baleful Strike, and Blaze keeps ticking after the trade.

edits.before: Level 2: still close — Veigar hasn't stacked enough Q for his burst to matter and you haven't unlocked W, so it stays skill-based.
edits.after: Level 2: Veigar has no stacks worth fearing yet and no dash at all, so your ablaze-into-stun threat already owns the wave.

edits.before: Pyroclasm bounces are hard to dodge for a champion with no dash, so your all-in threat spikes harder than his Primordial Burst (Q) stacking snowball at this point.
edits.after: Pyroclasm bounces are hard to dodge for a champion with no dash, so your all-in threat spikes harder than his Baleful Strike (Q) stacking, and his R is 120s at rank 1.

edits.before: His Dark Matter (R) execute threat on low-HP targets from range is real, but you still win most direct trades if he doesn't land a cage stun first.
edits.after: His Primordial Burst (R) grows with the health you are missing, so it is lethal when you are low, but you win most direct trades if the cage misses.

edits.before: With Luden's or Liandry's online your combo punishes any Event Horizon whiff instantly, and you generally win straight trades. His Dark Matter execute and stacked Q burst are genuine threats in teamfights if he gets a clean cage off, so you need to respect his engage rather than facetank it, but 1v1 you remain favored.
edits.after: With Luden's or Liandry's online your combo punishes any Event Horizon whiff instantly, and you generally win straight trades. His Primordial Burst and stacked Baleful Strike burst are genuine threats in a teamfight if he lands a clean cage, so respect that setup rather than facetank it, but 1v1 you remain favored.

edits.before: Use W to zone him off farm and deny his passive mana-into-AP stacking
edits.after: Use W to zone him off farm and deny his passive AP stacking off kills

edits.before: Look for Dark Matter execute picks in skirmishes once items are online
edits.after: Look for Primordial Burst picks in skirmishes once items are online

notes: Dark Matter is Veigar's W, not his R — the page used it as the name of his execute in spikes[3], the late text and wants.foe[3], and all three are fixed to Primordial Burst. suspectNames flagged exactly this and was right. The four full-layer rows that said Skill or Veigar disagreed with a content layer and packet chart that both said Brand on every row; sides moved and whys[0]/whys[1] rewritten because they argued 'even skill matchup' underneath a Brand row. Ratings left untouched: in this data the rating tracks stage intensity rather than ownership.
